summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with refractory multiple myeloma, MDS with pancytopenia, and COPD, was admitted for recurrent hypercalcemia with a calcium of 11.1 (corrected to 11.7) and new shortness of breath. He was treated with IV hydration and pamidronate, leading to normalization of calcium by discharge. A CT chest showed bronchial wall thickening and mucus plugging suggestive of chronic aspiration with possible infection, prompting a course of levofloxacin. Urinalysis showed abnormalities but cultures indicated contamination, so no UTI treatment was given. His atrial flutter and COPD were monitored, and medications were adjusted for safety, including reducing citalopram and modifying oxycodone. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient follow-up and lab monitoring.
